newsitem.title: USA: PanEnergy, Duke shareholders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: PanEnergy, Duke shareholders approve merger.

text.p: PanEnergy Corp and Duke Power Co shareholders in separate meetings on Thursday approved the proposed $7.7 billion merger of the companies, PanEnergy and Duke said.

The merger is awaiting final regulatory approval from the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and remains on track to close in the third quarter of this year, PanEnergy Chairman Paul Anderson said.
"We would expect a positive ruling due out some time in the next few months," Anderson told reporters after PanEnergy's shareholder meeting in Houston.

The proposed merger, approved earlier by state regulators, would form one of the largest U.S. energy and energy services companies ahead of expected deregulation of the country's electric industry, the companies said.

Under the agreement, each PanEnergy common share would be converted into the right to receive 1.0444 shares of Duke Power common stock. The new company, to be called Duke Energy, will be based in Charlotte.

The merged company plans to be a national energy wholesaler and form alliances to sell into retail markets opened to competition, said Anderson, who will become Duke Energy's president and chief operating officer.
